DirichletPadicLFunctions.reason: Retain the explicit rational-field arithmetic spine: Bernoulli/Mellin comparisons, Kubota–Leopoldt and all tame characters, branches/logarithmic values/poles, dyadic corrections, and the measure-valued Eisenstein expansion. Import existing classical carriers and the generic analytic suppliers; these arithmetic constructions are not already supplied by them.

AutomorphicPadicLFunctions.title: Dirichlet p-adic L-functions, special values, and Eisenstein measures, Part II: Ray-class and automorphic interpolation
AutomorphicPadicLFunctions.reason: DirichletPadicLFunctions is the first roadmap prerequisite. Its rational-field pseudomeasures, tame-character construction and Eisenstein measure are the boundary, not targets to construct again. Start beyond that boundary with global-unit descent on general ray-class limits, BSW GL2/F evaluation, Deligne–Ribet over totally real fields, ordinary Katz, and the distinct EHLS/Hsieh/Eischen–Wan branches; prove compatibility with the imported rational cases. Other geometric and modular-symbol suppliers remain prerequisites. The first-roadmap ordering does not add artificial dependencies between unrelated proof stages.

DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0.keeps: Own RJW Theorem 2.4's actual Mellin continuation argument, decay and differentiation proofs and its Bernoulli/smoothing application; compare the imported generalized Bernoulli quantities with complex L-values and prove algebraicity through chosen complex and p-adic embeddings. Reuse the already proved zeta(0) and negative-zeta, Gauss-inversion and character/conductor APIs. Own the explicit identification of the existing Dedekind series with AL.1's meromorphic germ, its simple-pole proof and equality of residue with the existing real class-number limit, without repeating the unit-volume calculation. Instantiate the imported rational idele/infinity-type dictionary in RJW 2.9/2.11 and prove normalization commutativity. All original positive and exceptional-conductor tests survive.
DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0.reason: Generalized Bernoulli and finite Fourier/Gauss data for character Eisenstein series belong to the existing ModularForms layer; classical Dirichlet continuation/conductor/Euler-factor interfaces belong to AN.1, general adelic continuation to AL.1, and idele characters/infinity types to GlobalNumberFields. Specific source proof routes and residue/embedding comparisons remain here. These supplier plans are not declarations that the missing parts are built.

DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1.keeps: Construct F_a(T)=1/T-a/((1+T)^a-1) integrally by cancellation for a>1 prime to p, instantiate the Amice inverse, and prove its moments, psi-invariance and the unit-restriction Euler factor. Construct x^-1 Res(mu_a), verify the regular-denominator and compatibility hypotheses of the shared pseudo-measure construction, and prove the resulting zeta_p is independent of a. Prove interpolation for every k>=1, keeping the k=1 zero Euler factor with zeta(0)=-1/2, odd-p parity/descent and smoothed/characterwise denominator-qualified Kummer congruences. Preserve the separate integral dyadic normalization and all scalar-extension maps.
DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1.reason: Import generic Mahler–Amice operators and localized pseudo-measure existence/evaluation instead of reimplementing them. Arithmetic cancellation, moment formulas and the actual smoothing-regularity witnesses remain here. Evaluation is only on the localization with nonvanishing character denominator, not every element of the total quotient ring.

DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2.keeps: Construct the actual p-power-character twists of the arithmetic measures and prove their roots-of-unity/Gauss calculation using the shared operator identities. Construct integral zeta_eta for primitive tame conductor D>1 prime to p; prove RJW 5.1/5.7, primitive-conductor evaluation at p, the separate trivial-character branch, coefficient-field descent/scalar extension, and primitive/imprimitive Euler-factor comparisons, including every exercise calculation in the existing contract.
DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2.reason: The generic twisting/restriction/roots-of-unity operators are supplied once by PM L2. Their arithmetic Gauss computation and all tame-character measures are retained here.

DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3.keeps: On the imported character components and compatible normalized logarithm, construct the Dirichlet branches and prove RJW 5.17/5.20. Own the complex cyclotomic-log L(1,chi) formula and Leopoldt's Theorem 6.1, including pure p-power conductor and exact Gauss/root-of-unity conventions. Prove Theorem 7.1's trivial-component pole, numerator evaluation, convergence, auxiliary log nonvanishing, division by its simple zero, residue 1-p^-1 in the specified s-coordinate and its coordinate-change law. Retain the integral p=2 construction with ±1 times (1+4Z_2). Export the k=1 formula to ColemanIntegration L3; do not import that later polylogarithm-value theorem.
DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3.reason: ColemanIntegration L0 supplies the common analytic log_p(p)=0 and branch-change theory; LAD L3 supplies analytic Mellin coordinates/component operations. This layer owns the specific L-value and residue formulas. The direction Coleman L0 -> Dirichlet L3 -> Coleman L3 avoids a circular positive-value proof.

DirichletPadicLFunctions:L4.keeps: Use the existing classical Eisenstein modular forms, their generalized Bernoulli/Fourier coefficient API and pinned level-one q-expansion. Own the p-stabilized form E_k-p^(k-1)E_k(pz) for even k>=4, its actual modular-form/q-expansion comparison, coefficient measures A_n=sum_{d|n,p not dividing d}delta_d and A_0=x*zeta_p/2, and coefficientwise specialization at x^(k-1). Own the measure-valued tame-character family and integral coefficient congruences, with exact primitive and p-stabilization normalizations. Full geometric affinoid realization/Hida–Coleman control remains PadicFamilies' separate task; no new classical nebentypus/Eisenstein carrier is defined.
DirichletPadicLFunctions:L4.reason: The existing ModularForms layer owns classical character Eisenstein series, their generalized Bernoulli/Gauss translation and exceptional-weight conventions. The new measure and its arithmetic congruences remain here and supply the rational Deligne–Ribet comparison.

DirichletPadicLFunctions:KU-zeta.reason: Retain the source-unit checkpoint, its L0/AL.1 aggregation and H KU-existing prerequisite, and every original consumer/edge. It is not a second zeta construction or a completion claim.

AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L0.keeps: Construct the inverse-limit ray-class quotient at fixed tame modulus and p-power conductor from the existing finite groups/maps; retain the closure of global units and torsion, and prove the dimension formula with the Leopoldt defect. Instantiate global reciprocity and the generic character/distribution constructions on that actual quotient. Construct algebraic/p-adic avatars through embeddings and prove compatibility with the imported complex characters, infinity types and conductors. Own finite-level evaluation, descent, norm/twist/tame-change maps and the conditional cohomological evaluation principle with actual lifts, norm relations and growth/uniqueness hypotheses; no universal existence axiom.
AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L0.reason: Finite ray groups, complex Hecke characters/infinity types and global Artin reciprocity have fixed Tau Ceti owners. PM L0a owns rigid representability/universal characters; PM L1 owns completed-group-ring measure algebra; LAD L3 supplies the analytic Mellin/evaluation refinement. The arithmetic inverse-limit quotient, unit descent and application-specific hypotheses are new, not a second copy of those foundations.

AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L1.keeps: Retain the imported arithmetic quotient, Borel–Serre, Hecke-local-system, automorphic-cohomology and GL2 L-function carriers. Own BSW's evaluation cycles in degree r1+r2, signs, rational/period structures and Theorem 5.7 over general F. Prove the F=Q identification with the existing modular-symbol period lines and critical-value formula, including orientation, character inverses, Gauss factors and all period choices; do not reconstruct the rational modular-symbol theorem.
AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L1.reason: The rational-field critical-value theorem is owned by ModularSymbols L1. General-field construction and the comparison of actual cycles/maps are retained, not replaced by a black-box abstract interpolation hypothesis.

AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L2.keeps: Construct BSW's distribution coefficient systems, actual specialized cohomology, eigenlifts, automorphic cycles and evaluations over F. Prove control for admissible (k,v), k+2v parallel, with h_q<(min_{sigma|q}k_sigma+v_q(lambda)+1)/e_q, normalized U_q, source p-level conditions and a coefficient field containing the embeddings/eigenvalues. Prove unit descent, distribution/norm relations, per-place growth and Theorem 11.1 with individually specified sign, discriminant, Gauss, refined-eigenvalue, period and Euler factors. Compare the constructed F=Q instance to imported modular symbols, and retain Hilbert/nonparallel-admissible and Bianchi tests. General-field families retain their cohomological-control/nonabelian-Leopoldt hypotheses; a single-form theorem does not prove them.
AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L2.reason: Import the rational small-slope/eigenlift/interpolation theorem and the group-independent compact-operator/Fredholm machinery. BSW's ramified, multivariable coefficient estimates and arithmetic control theorem remain new.

AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3.keeps: Own Deligne–Ribet over general totally real F: algebraicity of partial zeta values, Hilbert Eisenstein construction on canonical geometric objects, integral congruences, bounded denominators, smoothing and Euler factors. Import the rational zeta_p, all tame-character measures and Eisenstein measure from Dirichlet L1/L2/L4 and prove equality on the actual F=Q character domain with identical normalizations. Retain any Shintani realization as a proved computational comparison. For ordinary CM type, import CM abelian varieties/reflex data and the canonical geometric expansion/Igusa inputs; own the Katz-specific ordinary deformation/lift where not supplied, differential operators, CM periods, Eisenstein measure, critical-character evaluation and all required integral comparisons. Do not infer mixed-characteristic Igusa lifts from the special-fiber theorem, or extend Katz to nonordinary CM primes/all infinity types. Export one actual Deligne–Ribet object to IntegralIwasawa I.3, which owns its Stickelberger dictionary.
AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3.reason: The three distinct rational-field overlap leads all point from Dirichlet into this comparison, never in reverse. CM theory and generic geometric expansion/Igusa constructions have canonical owners. Missing Katz/Hilbert source-specific integral hypotheses stay explicit here rather than being declared supplied by a broader name.

AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3h.reason: Retain Hsieh published Theorems A–C and section 6 in full: actual toric test vectors, CM evaluations and square-root distribution, its square's central-value interpolation, squarefree n-minus and Hypothesis A root numbers, p-ordinary CM type without assuming pi ordinary, and every extra unramified-p/residual/character-image-order/conductor condition for mu=0 and nonvanishing. Preserve finite-exception versus higher-dimensional Zariski-density distinction and all congruence/GH/BSD consumers. Katz/EHLS do not replace this theorem.

AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4.keeps: Instantiate the canonical unitary PEL variety, bundles, compactifications, extensions, expansions and special-fiber Igusa tower in EHLS's exact datum; prove all additional source-specific mixed-characteristic ordinary lifts, coherent-cohomology/base-change/integrality conditions not supplied by those contracts. Own ordinary Hecke modules and pairings, differential operators, Eisenstein measure, doubling embedding, global identity and ramified/p-adic local calculations. Prove Main Theorem 9.2.2 for the stated anti-holomorphic cuspidal ordinary representation, tame type, coefficient modules and bases, retaining Hypotheses 7.3.2/7.3.3 and Proposition–Hypothesis 7.3.5. The output stays in the specified completed Iwasawa–Hecke/period-module tensor product with its congruence and local factors; no blanket freeness/Gorenstein/minimality assumption is discharged by generic geometry.
AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4.reason: Make the document's canonical-ownership instruction explicit at stage level: import existing geometry, then prove the EHLS-specific arithmetic construction and every additional integral instance. IG.1 supplies only its stated special-fiber/finite-level geometry, not a characteristic-zero ordinary tower by itself.

AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4e.reason: Retain the distinct Eischen–Wan arXiv:1404.7153v2 vector-valued finite-slope Klingen construction, auxiliary character/refinement/integral sections and exact local/global interpolation over the imaginary-quadratic field at odd split p. Theorem 5.8/Corollary 5.9's constant-term divisibility remains restricted to r=2. Preserve imports from PadicFamilies L2a and the outgoing L2/L2s/BSD.6a handoffs. Neither ordinary EHLS nor a general eigenvariety proves this construction; congruence/Galois-class arguments remain AutomorphicCongruences' work.

AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L5.keeps: Own comparisons of periods, coefficient extensions and primitive/imprimitive normalizations between all constructed analytic instances, and their relationship to L0's conditional evaluation principle. On Selmer L4's explicit realization/criticality data, define once the analytic Coates–Perrin-Riou/Panchishkin existence proposition with critical set, period/refinement/Panchishkin choices and the precise interpolation formula. Export this proposition to ModularIwasawaMainConjectures L5; its Greenberg/arithmetic-main-conjecture propositions and examples remain there. RJW Remark 13.24 remains context, not a universal noncommutative theorem. No existence constructor is introduced.
AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L5.reason: Shared realization/criticality and finite-versus-ordinary local-condition comparisons are imported, not redefined. Analytic existence is distinct from Selmer L4's RJW 13.21 arithmetic conjecture; identify their actual input records rather than identifying their conclusions.
